page: Microsoft Azure E8-2s_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine built on Microsoft Hyper-V, featuring a constrained-core architecture designed to reduce per-core licensing expenses. Powered by an Intel Xeon Platinum 8370C processor running at a base frequency of 2.8 GHz, this x86_64 instance allocates 2 dedicated vCPUs from a single physical core across two hardware threads. The processor includes 48 KB L1 data cache, 1 MB L2 cache, and 48 MB L3 cache, with hardware support for vector extensions including AVX-512 and cryptographic acceleration via AES and SHA-NI.

The instance provides an expansive memory allocation of 64.0 GB RAM, yielding an exceptionally high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 32 GB per virtual core. It does not include bundled local storage or integrated hardware GPUs, requiring persistent storage and operating system disks to be attached via remote block storage. Complimentary public IPv4 addresses are not provided by default.

Synthetic benchmarking demonstrates the performance impact of the constrained-core design. Single-threaded metrics, including a Geekbench single-core score of 1650.0 and a stress-ng single-core score of 1889.58, place the instance in the middle tier of general compute performance. However, with only two virtual cores active, parallel throughput is strictly limited. The multi-core Geekbench score sits at 1889.0, multi-core stress-ng reaches 1924.78, and PassMark database operations register at 1030.73. Memory throughput measures 14.49 GB/sec for uncached read operations and 13.45 GB/sec for uncached write operations, while PassMark memory testing registers an average score of 2081.57.

From a cost and architecture perspective, the E8-2s_v5 offers a specialized tradeoff by decoupling memory allocation from processing scale. By restricting the instance to two active cores within an eight-core memory footprint, it enables high-capacity memory usage while minimizing per-core software licensing costs. This configuration is best suited for memory-bound applications that require substantial working memory but modest computational power, such as lightweight in-memory caches, memory-intensive staging environments, and database engines constrained by core-based licensing models.
description: Microsoft Azure E8-2s_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine tailored for memory-intensive workloads that require modest CPU allocation. Powered by an Intel Xeon Platinum 8370C processor clocked at 2.8 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, this constrained-core instance exposes 2 dedicated vCPUs across 1 physical core alongside an expansive 64.0 GB of RAM. The instance does not feature bundled local storage or GPU acceleration, relying on remote volumes for persistence. Benchmark results reflect a 1:32 vCPU-to-memory ratio, demonstrating solid single-core metrics with an average Geekbench single-core score of 1650.0 and a stress-ng score of 1889.58, juxtaposed against constrained multi-core performance due to the low core count. The E8-2s_v5 provides high cost efficiency for workloads governed by per-core software licensing, serving as an effective platform for in-memory caching systems, smaller relational databases with extensive working sets, and memory-constrained analytical pipelines.
